relations.subject: Kurtis R. Schaeffer
relations.role: Professor of Tibetan and Buddhist Studies and Chair of the Religious Studies department
relations.evidence: Kurtis R. Schaeffer is Professor of Tibetan and Buddhist Studies at the University of Virginia, United States, and Chair of the Religious Studies department.

relations.subject: Kurtis R. Schaeffer
relations.evidence: Schaeffer received a B.A. in Religious Studies from Lewis & Clark College, Portland, Oregon in 1988

relations.subject: Kurtis R. Schaeffer
relations.evidence: and an additional B.A. from the Evergreen State College, Olympia, Washington, in 1990.

relations.subject: Kurtis R. Schaeffer
relations.role: Master of Arts (M.A.) in Buddhist Studies
relations.evidence: He received a Master of Arts (M.A.) in Buddhist Studies from the University of Washington in 1995

relations.subject: Kurtis R. Schaeffer
relations.role: Doctorate of Philosophy (PhD) in Tibetan and South Asian Religions
relations.evidence: and then a Doctorate of Philosophy (PhD) from Harvard University in 2000 in Tibetan and South Asian Religions.

relations.subject: Kurtis R. Schaeffer
relations.evidence: In 2000, he was appointed assistant professor at the University of Alabama in the Department of Religious Studies.

relations.subject: Kurtis R. Schaeffer
relations.evidence: Schaeffer was awarded tenure and promoted to the position of associate professor a year early, in 2004.

relations.subject: Kurtis R. Schaeffer
relations.evidence: In late 2005, Schaeffer took a position at the University of Virginia as an associate professor in the Department of Religious Studies

relations.subject: Kurtis R. Schaeffer
relations.role: co-director of the Tibetan and Himalayan Religious Group in the American Academy of Religion (AAR)
relations.evidence: He is also the past co-director, with Frances Garrett, of the Tibetan and Himalayan Religious Group in the American Academy of Religion (AAR).
